cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Expand Your Jurisdiction
cards.instruction: Use every new problem as a reason to expand what you are entitled to control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Accounts keeps missing tea because the kitchen's locked. Give me control of the keys, please; access has to be consistent.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here's a key, but the cleaners lock the kettle in their cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then their checklist is wrong. Send it to me for approval; equipment stays accessible after cleaning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Their contractor only takes instructions from the building manager.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then send me the manager's instructions before they go out. We can't fix a bad checklist by leaving its author unsupervised.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 checklist correction and A5 manager-instruction approval expand expert oversight from key control, but A5 calls manager checklist author without evidence.

responseLogic.evidence: B4 says manager instructs contractor, not that manager wrote cleaners checklist.

relationship.evidence: B2 supplies key and new obstacle; B4 supplies hierarchy detail, both practical contributions.

heightening.evidence: B4 manager route earns wider approval demand, but author label unnecessarily asserts who wrote the list.

specificity.evidence: A1 accounts tea and B2 locked kettle create clear small access problem.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 author-unsupervised maxim explains expansion through an unverified attribution.
